situation:
You are the brand manager for NORTHGATE ESPORTS, the regional leader in gaming and esports tournaments, which runs eighteen weekend events a year and is opening its first venue outside the state this fall. The vice president of operations (judge) has asked you to settle one question before the lease on that out-of-state arena is signed.

NORTHGATE built its name on tournaments families are comfortable sending a fourteen-year-old to, and about half the players in its registration database are under eighteen. Staff use that database to greet returning players by name, track their brackets, and message parents when a match time moves. The arena NORTHGATE wants, however, earns most of its own revenue from alcohol sales on event nights.

CROWN RIDGE BREWING will sponsor the expansion outright, covering the new venue's entire first year, provided beer is served in the main hall and its logo runs on the tournament broadcast. The regional school league, which has fed NORTHGATE teams for six years, has told its member schools it will not sanction play where beer is served, so those teams would stop entering, and floor staff would need identification-check training the company has never run.

Turning the sponsorship down keeps the school league and the family brand intact, but the expansion then comes out of the cash NORTHGATE set aside over three profitable years, and the arena has said it will book a competing organizer into the same weekend dates. Opening slowly in a market a rival is already entering carries a price of its own.

The vice president (judge) wants your analysis of how the sponsorship would change the business NORTHGATE has built, and a recommendation on which way to go. The vice president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of operations (judge) for NORTHGATE ESPORTS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have to sign or walk away from the out-of-state arena lease this month, and the sponsorship question decides which. You want to hear how the brand manager reads the effect on the business NORTHGATE has built, which way the recommendation goes, and how that decision would be delivered to the people it costs the most.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who does this decision land hardest on?
How would you explain it to them?
